Science notes

An interactive teaching resource on how neutral hydrogen between a distant quasar and us becomes the Lyman-α forest: atoms meet light, light stretches, gas maps to velocity, optical depth adds, transmitted light multiplies, and the forest can be read backward only up to a point. These notes list, for every scientific claim the scenes make, its sources, the assumptions under which it holds, the simplifications made for teaching, and how the browser's numbers were checked.

what is modeledwhat is nottoy and realthe claims, in six chapters7 · validation and accuracyby scenereferencescite

What is modeled

  • Lyman-α absorption by neutral hydrogen: the 1s → 2p resonance Lyα (H I 1s → 2p) transition data, met in each atom's own frame Resonance in the atom's frame (Doppler condition), removes light from the beam by scattering it in other directions Lyα "absorption" in the IGM is resonant scattering out of the beam.
  • Line shapes: thermal Doppler broadening Doppler parameter and the thermal (Gaussian) profile, natural broadening from the lifetime of the 2p level Natural broadening from the finite lifetime of 2p, and their combination, the Voigt profile The Voigt profile — normalisation, definition and asymptotics.
  • From gas to spectrum: cosmological redshift Cosmological redshift stretches every wavelength by the same factor; the map from real space to velocity space, u = aH(z)·x + v_pec Real space → velocity space map; optical depth accumulated along the sightline Line-of-sight accumulation of optical depth in velocity space, which adds Why optical depths add; and transmitted flux F = e^−τ Transmitted flux (Beer–Lambert), which saturates Saturation and the curve of growth.
  • Observation and inference: a spectrograph's resolution and noise act on the recorded flux Instrument resolution acts on the observed flux Noise model and signal-to-noise; several arrangements of gas can record the same line The "same shadow" configurations, and further information can break the tie What breaks the degeneracy.

What the teaching app does not model

  • No hydrodynamics. The gas is a toy Zel'dovich volume The toy Zel'dovich volume (synthetic teaching data), not an evolved simulation: temperature follows a power-law temperature–density relation and the velocities follow linear theory; nothing is computed from a thermal or dynamical history.
  • Neutral hydrogen is set by photoionisation equilibrium in a uniform ultraviolet background Photoionisation equilibrium and the neutral-amount control. There is no transfer of ionising radiation, no self-shielding and no collisional ionisation; the scene that changes the neutral amount holds density and temperature fixed.
  • One velocity and one temperature per sampling element One velocity per sampling element (unresolved velocity structure is not represented): velocity structure smaller than a cell is not represented.
  • Only Lyman-α is drawn, except in the last scene, where Lyman-β and a heavier-ion line appear as extra information. There is no continuum fitting, no quasar proximity effect, and the fine structure of Lyman-α is below every width shown Lyα (H I 1s → 2p) transition data.
  • Teaching representations are marked as such where they appear: atoms are a representative sample Representative atoms are a cartoon sample, parcels are a decomposition of a continuous sightline Parcels are a teaching decomposition of a continuous sightline, and the natural width is magnified wherever it is drawn Natural width is magnified wherever it is drawn.

Toy, oracles and data

The teaching toy
Every scene draws from one small synthetic data set: a 20 Mpc/h Zel'dovich volume at z = 3 (a 20 × 8 × 8 Mpc/h block of it is drawn) and one sightline through it The toy Zel'dovich volume (synthetic teaching data), decomposed for teaching into parcels and cells Parcels are a teaching decomposition of a continuous sightline. It is not a hydrodynamic simulation and contains no data from any survey or simulation suite.
Numerical oracles
Independent calculations check the browser's physics: SciPy's Faddeeva function for the Voigt profile, exact-Voigt optical-depth sums, numerical integration of distances, and the fake_spectra code for the real-space method. Their results are listed under Accuracy.
Simulation data, later
The skewer interface The skewer interface (dataset-independent) is independent of the data set, so a later release may replace the toy with simulation skewers whose conventions match fake_spectra fake_spectra conventions (the later validation target). No such data are included in this release.

The claims, in six chapters

Each claim states what the app teaches, its sources at their exact location, its assumptions and validity, the simplifications made for teaching, and how its numbers are checked. Read in order, the chapters follow the story of the app: one atom, one line, the expanding universe, many contributions, the gas itself, and the inverse problem.

1 · Lyα: one atom and the colour it absorbs

What a single hydrogen atom does to the quasar's light: the Lyα transition, resonance in the atom's own frame, and resonant scattering out of the beam.

¶ Lyα (H I 1s → 2p) transition data

Neutral hydrogen in its ground state resonantly absorbs Lyα photons at a rest (vacuum) wavelength of 1215.67 Å, with absorption oscillator strength f ≈ 0.4164; the 2p level decays back to 1s with Einstein coefficient A21 ≈ 6.26×10⁸ s⁻¹, i.e. a lifetime ≈ 1.6 ns.

λ0=1215.6701 A˚ (vacuum),f12=0.4164,A21=6.2649×108 s−1\lambda_0 = 1215.6701\ \text{Å (vacuum)},\quad f_{12} = 0.4164,\quad A_{21} = 6.2649\times10^{8}\ {\rm s^{-1}}λ0​=1215.6701 A˚ (vacuum),f12​=0.4164,A21​=6.2649×108 s−1
Convention
λ0 = 1215.6701 Å is NIST's unresolved 1s–2 multiplet value (its upper level includes 2s); the gf-weighted 2p centre is 1215.67004 Å (0.015 km/s different). The ~1.3 km/s fine-structure splitting (1215.6736 / 1215.6682 Å) is below every width the resource shows and is not taught.
Assumptions
  • vacuum wavelengths; fine structure unresolved; ground-state population only
Valid for
all IGM conditions considered (A₂₁ far exceeds the collisional and photo-excitation rates at IGM densities, so n = 2 is essentially empty)
Sources
  • NIST ASD (Kramida et al. 2024) — H I lines output 1215–1216 Å (2p3/2, 2p1/2, unresolved 1s–2)
  • Wiese & Fuhr 2009 — Table 6, entry 1, p. 578 (λ 1215.67 Å, A = 6.2649e8 s⁻¹, f = 0.41641, g 2–6)

¶ Resonance in the atom's frame (Doppler condition)

An atom moving with line-of-sight velocity v sees incoming light Doppler-shifted; it is resonant with light whose observed (lab-frame) wavelength is λ0(1 + v/c) to first order in v/c. An atom moving away from the observer (v > 0, toward the quasar) therefore absorbs a redder colour.

λres=λ0 (1+v/c)+O(v2/c2)\lambda_{\rm res} = \lambda_0\,(1 + v/c) + \mathcal{O}(v^2/c^2)λres​=λ0​(1+v/c)+O(v2/c2)
Convention
same sign as Peculiar-velocity sign convention
Assumptions
  • non-relativistic speeds (v/c ≲ 10⁻³)
Valid for
v ≪ c
Simplifications
  • The resonance window is drawn ~500× wider than the natural width (see Natural width is magnified wherever it is drawn).
Sources
  • Rybicki & Lightman 1979 — §10.6 Line Broadening Mechanisms — Doppler broadening, p. 287

¶ Natural broadening from the finite lifetime of 2p

Because the 2p state has a finite lifetime (1/A21 ≈ 1.6 ns), even a stationary atom's response is a Lorentzian with half-width γ = Γλ0/4π ≈ 0.0061 km/s, Γ = A21 (2p decays only to 1s). This is ~2000× narrower (FWHM) than the thermal width at 10⁴ K, but falls off only as 1/Δv².

γ=Γλ04π=6.06×10−3 km s−1,a=γ/b\gamma = \frac{\Gamma\lambda_0}{4\pi} = 6.06\times10^{-3}\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}},\qquad a = \gamma/bγ=4πΓλ0​​=6.06×10−3 kms−1,a=γ/b
Convention
Γ is the total decay rate out of the upper level (the lower level is the ground state, width 0)
Assumptions
  • radiative damping only; collisional (pressure) broadening negligible at IGM densities
Valid for
IGM densities (n ≲ 10⁻² cm⁻³)
Simplifications
  • The damped oscillation (microscope only, labelled) is the classical Lorentz-oscillator analogue; the physical statement is the finite lifetime.
  • The natural line is magnified ×1200 in the inset (Natural width is magnified wherever it is drawn).
Sources
  • Rybicki & Lightman 1979 — §10.6 — natural broadening (Lorentzian)
How it is checked

¶ Photoionisation equilibrium and the neutral-amount control

In the highly ionised IGM, photoionisation balances recombination: n_HI Γ_HI = α(T) n_e n_p, so n_HI ≈ α(T) n_e n_H / Γ_HI ∝ Δ² T^(−0.7) / Γ_HI. Changing the UV background rescales n_HI (and τ) by 1/Γ_HI; it does not move lines or change their τ-shape.

nHI≃αA(T) ne nHΓHI,αA≃4.2×10−13 (T/104 K)−0.7 cm3 s−1n_{\rm HI} \simeq \frac{\alpha_A(T)\,n_e\,n_{\rm H}}{\Gamma_{\rm HI}},\qquad \alpha_A \simeq 4.2\times10^{-13}\,(T/10^4\,{\rm K})^{-0.7}\ {\rm cm^3\,s^{-1}}nHI​≃ΓHI​αA​(T)ne​nH​​,αA​≃4.2×10−13(T/104K)−0.7 cm3s−1
Convention
case-A recombination (optically thin IGM); n_e = 1.163 n_H (H and He fully ionised, Y_P = 0.2454, Planck 2018)
Assumptions
  • ionisation equilibrium (recombination time ≪ Hubble time is NOT true at mean density; equilibrium is still set by photoionisation, which is fast)
  • He fully ionised (n_e/n_H = 1.081 with helium singly ionised to 1.163 fully ionised, for Y_P = 0.2454; a 7 % systematic)
Valid for
n_HI ≪ n_H (forest; not self-shielded LLS/DLAs)
Simplifications
  • The teaching control changes N_HI directly, holding density, temperature and position fixed; real UV changes also heat the gas.
Sources

2 · The line profile: thermal core and natural wings

How motion and the excited state's short life shape one absorption line — the Gaussian census, the Lorentzian wings, their Voigt combination and how the browser computes it.

¶ Maxwellian velocities; one line-of-sight component is Gaussian

In gas at temperature T each Cartesian velocity component of the atoms follows a Gaussian with variance kT/m. The beam is sensitive only to the component along it.

f(v∥)=m2πkT  e−mv∥2/2kTf(v_\parallel) = \sqrt{\frac{m}{2\pi kT}}\;e^{-m v_\parallel^2/2kT}f(v∥​)=2πkTm​​e−mv∥2​/2kT
Convention
v_∥ along the sightline, positive away from the observer
Assumptions
  • thermal equilibrium of the atoms' motions; no turbulence
Valid for
IGM gas (collisional thermalisation of velocities is fast compared with dynamical times)
Simplifications
  • A few hundred representative atoms stand in for ~10⁶⁶ (Representative atoms are a cartoon sample).
Sources
  • Rybicki & Lightman 1979 — §10.6 Line Broadening Mechanisms — Doppler broadening, p. 287
  • Draine 2011 — ch. 6, §6.3–6.4 (Doppler broadening; Lyα f = 0.4164 as corrected) (secondary)
How it is checked

the micro view samples N atoms from the Maxwellian and overlays the analytic curve

used in 3 · Temperature becomes line width · status: verified · id SCI-THERM-001

¶ Doppler parameter and the thermal (Gaussian) profile

The census of line-of-sight speeds is the line's thermal profile: a Gaussian in Δv of width b = √(2kT/m), normalised so that heating spreads the same absorption over more velocities without adding any. b(10⁴ K) = 12.85 km/s for hydrogen.

b=2kT/mH+bturb2,ϕG(Δv)=e−Δv2/b2π bb = \sqrt{2kT/m_{\rm H} + b_{\rm turb}^2},\qquad \phi_{\rm G}(\Delta v) = \frac{e^{-\Delta v^2/b^2}}{\sqrt{\pi}\,b}b=2kT/mH​+bturb2​​,ϕG​(Δv)=π​be−Δv2/b2​
Convention
m = mass of the ¹H atom (1.00782503 u = 1.6735328×10⁻²⁴ g; an earlier value, 1.6735575×10⁻²⁴ g, was corrected — a 1.5×10⁻⁵ effect); b_turb = 0 unless stated. (fake_spectra's mass convention is recorded in fake_spectra conventions (the later validation target).)
Assumptions
  • Maxwellian velocities (Maxwellian velocities; one line-of-sight component is Gaussian)
Valid for
all thermal widths considered
Simplifications
  • Turbulent / unresolved bulk motion inside a parcel is ignored in the toy (b_turb = 0); in real lines it adds in quadrature.
  • Beat 3 isolates the intrinsic thermal Doppler width. A real absorber's line is also widened by velocity variation across the extended gas — the Hubble flow and its own motions across its size (Parcels are a teaching decomposition of a continuous sightline, shown in Beat 6) — and the recorded line by the instrument (Instrument resolution acts on the observed flux, Beat 11). A line width alone is therefore not a thermometer (The "same shadow" configurations).
Sources
  • Rybicki & Lightman 1979 — §10.6 Line Broadening Mechanisms — Doppler broadening, p. 287
  • Draine 2011 — ch. 6, §6.3–6.4 (secondary)
  • Meiksin 2009 — §II.A, Eqs. (10)–(11): b = (2kT/m_a)^½; a kinematic component adds in quadrature (secondary)

¶ The Voigt profile — normalisation, definition and asymptotics

The line profile is the convolution of the thermal Gaussian with the natural Lorentzian (each atom's Lorentzian at each atom's Doppler shift). In velocity units φ(Δv) = H(a, Δv/b)/(√π b), with H(a,x) = Re w(x + ia) and ∫H dx = √π. For a ≪ 1 the core is ≈ e^(−x²) and the far wings ≈ a/(√π x²): core from motion, wings from lifetime.

H(a,x)=aπ∫−∞∞e−y2 dy(x−y)2+a2,ϕ(Δv)=H(a,Δv/b)π bH(a,x) = \frac{a}{\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{e^{-y^2}\,dy}{(x-y)^2 + a^2},\qquad \phi(\Delta v) = \frac{H(a,\Delta v/b)}{\sqrt{\pi}\,b}H(a,x)=πa​∫−∞∞​(x−y)2+a2e−y2dy​,ϕ(Δv)=π​bH(a,Δv/b)​
H(a,x)≃e−x2+aπ x2(a≪1)H(a,x) \simeq e^{-x^2} + \frac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}\,x^2}\quad (a \ll 1)H(a,x)≃e−x2+π​x2a​(a≪1)
Convention
x = Δv/b, a = γ/b
Assumptions
  • Doppler parameter and the thermal (Gaussian) profile, Natural broadening from the finite lifetime of 2p act independently (impact approximation not needed)
Valid for
all a considered; the two-term asymptotic is a teaching approximation, not used in computation
Simplifications
  • The micro view exaggerates the damping parameter (labelled, ×1–1000).
Sources
  • Rybicki & Lightman 1979 — §10.6 — combined Doppler and Lorentz profiles (Voigt)
  • Meiksin 2009 — §II.A, Eqs. (9)–(13): Voigt = Lorentzian ⊗ Maxwellian; H(a,x); a

¶ Numerical Voigt implementation in the app

The app evaluates H(a,x) with Humlicek's (1982) W4 rational approximation at all (a, x). Against the Faddeeva function (SciPy's wofz) it is accurate to < 10⁻⁴ (relative) over a ∈ [10⁻⁶, 1], |x| ≤ 2×10⁴ (measured values in Voigt function accuracy). The Tepper-García (2006) approximation was tested and rejected: 2–6 % errors for 2 < |x| < 6.

Valid for
a ∈ [1e-6, 1], |x| ≤ 2e4
Sources
  • Humlíček 1982 — algorithm W4 (regions I–IV): all 29 coefficients and 4 border constants are identical, digit by digit, in five independent open-source transcriptions that cite Humlicek 1982 (RFM, ExoCross, SKIRT 9, SOCRATES, monoRTM). The original paper was not consulted; the accuracy authority is SciPy's Faddeeva function (wofz), against which [[#check-voigt-001|Voigt function accuracy]] tests every region, including the tiny-a regime Zaghloul (2015) flags
  • Zaghloul 2015 — Table 1 (original borders of the regions), p. 3, arXiv:1505.05596v1 — matches the app's region borders (secondary)

¶ Saturation and the curve of growth

Once τ0 ≳ 3 the line core transmits almost nothing and the line's depth stops measuring N; its equivalent width then grows only logarithmically (∝ b√ln τ0) until the damping wings pass τ = 1, after which W ∝ √(N γ). In τ the profile shape never changes; only in F does the line change character.

W∝N (τ0≪1);W∝bln⁡τ0 (flat);W∝Nγ (damped)W \propto N\ (\tau_0 \ll 1);\quad W \propto b\sqrt{\ln\tau_0}\ (\text{flat});\quad W \propto \sqrt{N\gamma}\ (\text{damped})W∝N (τ0​≪1);W∝blnτ0​​ (flat);W∝Nγ​ (damped)
Assumptions
  • single Voigt line
Valid for
isolated lines
Sources
  • Draine 2011 — ch. 9 Absorption Lines: The Curve of Growth (p. 75 ff.)

¶ Where damping wings become visible

From the Lorentzian asymptote, τ(Δv) ≈ Nσ_vγ/(πΔv²), so the wing reaches τ = 1 at Δv ≈ √(Nσ_vγ/π) ≈ 160 km/s (N/10¹⁹ cm⁻²)^½, independent of b (this algebra is ours, from the far-wing profile in Meiksin 2009). For forest lines (N ≲ 10¹⁵) this lies inside the Doppler core: their wings are invisible. The wings become detectable only in rare absorbers of very high column density (high N_HI).

Δvτ=1≈Nσvγ/π\Delta v_{\tau=1} \approx \sqrt{N\sigma_v\gamma/\pi}Δvτ=1​≈Nσv​γ/π​
Assumptions
  • a ≪ 1
Valid for
damping wings become detectable from N ≳ 10^18.5 (≈ 3×10¹⁸) cm⁻² and set the line's width at τ = 1 above about 10¹⁹ cm⁻² (the sources below); the asymptote assumes a ≪ 1
Sources
  • Meiksin 2009 — §II.A, Eqs. (6), (12)–(13) and the text before Eq. (26) (arXiv v3 p. 9): far from line centre φ_V ≃ a/(πx²); §II.B.1 (p. 9): forest systems are well fit by Doppler profiles, DLAs show the damping wings
  • Rauch 1998 — §3.4 (arXiv v1 p. 15): 'From N ≳ 10^18.5 on, the damping wings of Lyα become detectable'
  • Wolfe, Gawiser & Prochaska 2005 — §1.1 (arXiv v2 p. 4): unit optical depth in the damping wings at Δν_τ=1 ∝ [A21 f21 N(H I)]^1/2 when N(H I) > 10^19 cm⁻² (secondary)

3 · Cosmological coordinates: redshift, distance and velocity space

How the expanding universe stretches the light, how real-space distance and peculiar motion map to observed velocity and wavelength, and the conventions used for both.

¶ Cosmological redshift stretches every wavelength by the same factor

Light absorbed by gas at redshift z_abs at rest-frame wavelength λ_rest (1215.67 Å for Lyα, in the gas's own frame) reaches us at λ_obs = λ_rest (1 + z_abs), where 1 + z_abs = a(t_obs)/a(t_abs). Every wavelength, and every wavelength interval, is multiplied by the same factor. The reverse operation, λ_rest = λ_obs/(1 + z_abs), re-expresses the observed spectrum in the absorber's rest frame: there the absorber's own line is at exactly 1215.67 Å. (In the quasar's rest frame, λ_obs/(1 + z_q), the same absorption lies blueward of 1215.67 Å — The quasar's frame — why the forest lies blueward of the quasar's own Lyα.)

λobs=λrest(1+z),1+z=λobsλrest=a(tobs)a(tem),λrest=λobs1+z\lambda_{\rm obs} = \lambda_{\rm rest}(1+z),\qquad 1+z = \frac{\lambda_{\rm obs}}{\lambda_{\rm rest}} = \frac{a(t_{\rm obs})}{a(t_{\rm em})},\qquad \lambda_{\rm rest} = \frac{\lambda_{\rm obs}}{1+z}λobs​=λrest​(1+z),1+z=λrest​λobs​​=a(tem​)a(tobs​)​,λrest​=1+zλobs​​
Convention
Three frames are kept distinct: the absorber's rest frame (where the atom sees 1215.67 Å), the observer's frame (us), and the quasar's rest frame (The quasar's frame — why the forest lies blueward of the quasar's own Lyα). "Measured at a point along the path" means by an observer at rest with the cosmic expansion there (comoving), for whom λ ∝ a.
Assumptions
  • FLRW expansion; comoving observers; the gas's own small motion folded into z_abs here
Valid for
any z; the beat uses 0 ≤ z_abs < z_q = 3.2 with z = 3 as the default (the toy's redshift)
Simplifications
  • Redshift is presented as the stretching of the light's wavelength with the expansion (λ ∝ a); the Doppler-vs-expansion interpretation debate is not raised.
Sources
  • Hogg 1999 — §3 'Redshift', Eq. (8): z = λ_o/λ_e − 1; Eq. (12): 1 + z = a(t_o)/a(t_e)

¶ The quasar's frame — why the forest lies blueward of the quasar's own Lyα

The quasar at z_q emits its own Lyα at 1215.67 Å in its frame, observed at 1215.67 (1 + z_q) Å. Gas between us and the quasar (z_abs < z_q) absorbs at 1215.67 (1 + z_abs) Å observed, i.e. at 1215.67 (1 + z_abs)/(1 + z_q) < 1215.67 Å in the quasar's rest frame: the Lyα forest lies blueward of the quasar's Lyα emission.

Convention
Cosmological redshift stretches every wavelength by the same factor
Assumptions
  • absorbers lie between us and the quasar
Valid for
z_abs < z_q
Simplifications
  • The quasar's emission line is drawn as a smooth bump on a flat continuum; its real shape and the proximity zone are not shown.
Sources
  • Meiksin 2009 — §II.A 'Resonance absorption lines', text preceding Eq. (15) (arXiv v3 p. 7); §I, p. 2 (absorption shortward of the QSO's Lyα)
  • Hogg 1999 — §3, Eq. (13): 1 + z₁₂ = (1 + z₂)/(1 + z₁)

¶ On a logarithmic ruler a stretch is a slide; small slides are velocities

Because the stretch multiplies every wavelength by (1 + z), it adds the same amount, ln(1 + z), to every ln λ. Small differences in ln λ are velocities, Δu = c Δln λ; this is the velocity coordinate u used from Beat 6 on, with λ_obs = λ0 (1 + z0) e^(u/c) (Velocity coordinate ↔ observed wavelength).

ln⁡λobs=ln⁡λrest+ln⁡(1+z),u=c ln⁡1+zabs1+z0\ln\lambda_{\rm obs} = \ln\lambda_{\rm rest} + \ln(1+z),\qquad u = c\,\ln\frac{1+z_{\rm abs}}{1+z_0}lnλobs​=lnλrest​+ln(1+z),u=cln1+z0​1+zabs​​
Convention
Velocity coordinate ↔ observed wavelength (log-λ, kept once defined)
Valid for
exact (identity)

¶ Comoving distance along the light's path (Planck 2018)

The line-of-sight comoving distance to redshift z is χ(z) = (c/H0) ∫0^z dz'/E(z'), E = (Ωm(1+z)³ + ΩΛ)^½ for flat ΛCDM; with Planck 2018 parameters χ(3) ≈ 4384 Mpc/h. It places the gas and the travelling light along the drawn path in Beat 5, and gives the distance to us printed beside the volume (Beats 0, 1, 11, 12), where the beam is broken because the 20 Mpc/h sample is about 0.5 % of that distance.

χ(z)=cH0∫0zdz′E(z′)\chi(z) = \frac{c}{H_0}\int_0^z \frac{dz^{\prime}}{E(z^{\prime})}χ(z)=H0​c​∫0z​E(z′)dz′​
Convention
Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing (Ωm = 0.3153, ΩΛ = 0.6847, h = 0.6736); radiation neglected (≲ 10⁻³ of E at z ≲ 4)
Assumptions
  • flat ΛCDM
Valid for
0 ≤ z ≤ 6 tested
Simplifications
  • The path is drawn to scale in comoving distance, so equal stretches do not cover equal lengths of path.

¶ The forest is written along the way

As the quasar's light travels, its wavelength measured by local comoving observers grows, λ_here = λ_emit (1 + z_q)/(1 + z_here). Each intervening hydrogen structure at z_abs absorbs the part of the spectrum that is at 1215.67 Å in its own frame — the part emitted at λ_emit = 1215.67 (1 + z_abs)/(1 + z_q) — and that shadow then stretches on with the light, reaching us at 1215.67 (1 + z_abs). Structures at different redshifts therefore cast shadows at different observed wavelengths, ordered by redshift, all blueward of the quasar's own Lyα at 1215.67 (1 + z_q): the Lyα forest.

λhere=λemit 1+zq1+zhere,λemit=1215.67 A˚ 1+zabs1+zq ⇒ λobs=1215.67 A˚ (1+zabs)\lambda_{\rm here} = \lambda_{\rm emit}\,\frac{1+z_{\rm q}}{1+z_{\rm here}},\qquad \lambda_{\rm emit} = 1215.67\,\text{Å}\,\frac{1+z_{\rm abs}}{1+z_{\rm q}}\ \Rightarrow\ \lambda_{\rm obs} = 1215.67\,\text{Å}\,(1+z_{\rm abs})λhere​=λemit​1+zhere​1+zq​​,λemit​=1215.67A˚1+zq​1+zabs​​ ⇒ λobs​=1215.67A˚(1+zabs​)
Convention
Cosmological redshift stretches every wavelength by the same factor; one redshift per structure (peculiar motion folded in, separated in Real space → velocity space map)
Assumptions
  • absorbers between us and the quasar; Lyα only
Valid for
z_abs < z_q
Simplifications
  • Lyβ and higher Lyman lines, the Lyman limit, and the atmospheric cut-off are not drawn.
Sources

  • Hogg 1999 — §3, Eq. (13): 1 + z₁₂ = (1 + z₂)/(1 + z₁)

Gas at comoving position x along the sightline, with line-of-sight peculiar velocity v_pec, absorbs at velocity coordinate u = aH(z) x_com + v_pec. Across a box of tens of Mpc/h the expansion rate is treated as constant.

¶ Peculiar-velocity sign convention

v_pec > 0 means the gas moves away from the observer (toward the quasar, +x); it lands at larger u, i.e. at a longer observed wavelength (redder). This is the same sign as the resonance condition Resonance in the atom's frame (Doppler condition).

4 · Optical depth, transmission and observation

Why optical depths add while transmitted light multiplies, what saturation does, and what an instrument changes — the record, not the gas.

¶ Lyα "absorption" in the IGM is resonant scattering out of the beam

After excitation to 2p the atom decays radiatively (A21 ≫ collisional and photo-excitation rates at IGM densities), re-emitting a Lyα photon in an essentially random direction. For a narrow beam from a point source this removes the photon from the line of sight; scattering of other photons into the beam is negligible. The beam's extinction therefore obeys the same e^−τ law as true absorption.

1s+γLyα→2p→1s+γ (random direction)1s + \gamma_{\rm Ly\alpha} \to 2p \to 1s + \gamma\ (\text{random direction})1s+γLyα​→2p→1s+γ (random direction)
Convention
Say "scattered out of our beam" in Beat 2 and again in Beat 5, where "shadow" is introduced; "removed"/"absorbed" elsewhere as shorthand.
Assumptions
  • point source; beam solid angle ≪ 4π; negligible re-scattering into the beam
Valid for
quasar sightlines through the diffuse IGM
Simplifications
  • Later beats say "absorbed" for brevity.
Sources
  • Meiksin 2009 — §I footnote 7; §II.A opening (features are scattering of resonance photons out of the line of sight)
  • Dijkstra 2014 — §4 Lyα Radiative Transfer Basics, opening paragraph; §5.2 (secondary)

¶ Line-of-sight accumulation of optical depth in velocity space

The optical depth at velocity u is the sum (integral) over all neutral hydrogen along the sightline of each element's profile centred on its own u(x): τ(u) = ∫ n_HI σ_v φ(u − u(x); b(x)) dx_prop. Discretised on cells it is Σ_j N_j σ_v φ(u − u_j; b_j).

¶ Discretisation limits — pixel size, pixel averaging and the periodic box

The cell sum is accurate only when (i) real-space pixels are finer than the narrowest line (aH·Δx ≤ b_min/2); (ii) one states whether a pixel's value is its centre τ, its mean τ or its mean F, since these differ for lines narrower than a pixel; and (iii) damping wings of strong absorbers are not cut by the periodic box.

aH Δx≤bmin⁡/2,⟨e−τ⟩pix≠e−⟨τ⟩pixaH\,\Delta x \le b_{\min}/2,\qquad \langle e^{-\tau}\rangle_{\rm pix} \ne e^{-\langle\tau\rangle_{\rm pix}}aHΔx≤bmin​/2,⟨e−τ⟩pix​=e−⟨τ⟩pix​
Convention
the app's default = point sampling of τ at pixel centres on a uniform u grid; nearest periodic image per cell
Valid for
Closure against fake_spectra: lines narrower than a coarse pixel are wrong by up to 0.46 in F (EW +93 %); oversampling to aH·Δx ≤ b/2 with exact pixel averaging brings this to 0.019. Mean τ vs mean F per pixel differ by ≥ 7×10⁻³ at 10 km/s pixels, and by up to 0.3 for narrow saturated lines. Both codes truncate wings at half a box: for an LLS/DLA, F changes by up to 0.28 and EW by 10 % against a true periodic sum. None of these occur in the toy at its sampling.

¶ Why optical depths add

Optical depth is the path integral of the opacity; the opacity of independent absorbers (here: different gas elements at the same observed velocity) adds linearly because each atom's absorption is independent of the others and of the radiation field (no stimulated emission, no saturation of the level populations). Flux decrements do not add.

τ(u)=∑iτi(u)\tau(u) = \sum_i \tau_i(u)τ(u)=i∑​τi​(u)
Assumptions
  • linear (optically passive) medium; ground-state populations unaffected by the beam
Valid for
IGM / quasar beams
Sources
  • Rybicki & Lightman 1979 — §1.4, Eqs. (1.26)–(1.30): dτ = α ds

¶ Transmitted flux (Beer–Lambert)

With no emission into the beam along the path, the transmitted fraction of the quasar's light is F = e^(−τ). F is the observed spectrum divided by the quasar's unabsorbed (continuum) spectrum.

F(u)=e−τ(u)F(u) = e^{-\tau(u)}F(u)=e−τ(u)
Convention
continuum-normalised flux, 0 ≤ F ≤ 1
Assumptions
  • no source term in the beam; continuum known
Valid for
quasar sightlines
Simplifications
  • The quasar continuum is divided out and never drawn (continuum fitting is out of scope).
Sources
  • Rybicki & Lightman 1979 — §1.4 Absorption Only, Eq. (1.25), p. 12

¶ Instrument resolution acts on the observed flux

A spectrograph records the transmitted flux convolved with its line-spread function, approximated as a Gaussian (we quote its FWHM in km/s; P1D analyses often quote the rms width, e.g. Palanque-Delabrouille et al. 2013 Eq. 6). Resolution changes neither the gas nor its optical depth — only the recorded spectrum.

Fobs(u)=∫F(u′) LSF(u−u′) du′ (+ noise)F_{\rm obs}(u) = \int F(u^{\prime})\,{\rm LSF}(u-u^{\prime})\,du^{\prime}\ (+\ \text{noise})Fobs​(u)=∫F(u′)LSF(u−u′)du′ (+ noise)

5 · The gas and how it is represented: a continuous sightline

The intergalactic gas itself — density, ionisation, temperature — and the teaching representations (volume, atoms, parcels, cells) that stand for it, with the toy data behind them.

¶ One velocity per sampling element (unresolved velocity structure is not represented)

A real-space skewer gives each sampling element (pixel) one peculiar velocity and one temperature. If the gas inside one element has several velocities — in particle codes, several SPH particles or kernel contributions moving differently that overlap the same pixel — that sub-element velocity structure is not represented, and its absorption is placed at one velocity instead of being spread over several.

¶ Exporting skewers from fake_spectra 2.2.4 — a velocity-convention compatibility note

During compatibility testing, the velocity returned through the tested export path — fake_spectra 2.2.4, Spectra.get_velocity on a Gadget-format snapshot — differed from the convention this resource requires (the proper peculiar velocity in km/s, Comoving vs physical coordinates and h-units). On a mock snapshot at a = 0.25 with known particle velocities, the returned value was 0.5 of the true peculiar velocity for every moving particle, equal to √a — consistent with the √a unit conversion being applied once more than this convention needs. The resource therefore never takes skewer velocities from that path: it constructs the line-of-sight velocity independently from the stored quantities (the toy from its displacement field). Two other observations on the same version, for anyone exporting skewers: turn_off_selfshield also set Γ_HI to zero, and get_velocity and HDF5Snapshot.get_npart needed a float32 workaround under NumPy 2.

¶ The toy Zel'dovich volume (synthetic teaching data)

The 3D gas, sightline and parcels in this resource come from a declared toy, not a simulation: a 256³ Zel'dovich displacement of a Gaussian field over 20 Mpc/h (P(k) ∝ k⁻² e^(−k²R²), R = 0.075 Mpc/h, ψ_rms = 0.36 Mpc/h), linear peculiar velocities v = f aHψ with f = Ω_m(z)^0.55 (no free velocity scaling), T = T0 Δ^(γ−1) with T0 = 1.3×10⁴ K, γ = 1.5, Planck 2018 cosmology, and n_HI from Photoionisation equilibrium and the neutral-amount control. Γ_HI is tuned so ⟨F⟩ = 0.68 on the chosen sightline (Mean transmitted flux at z ≈ 3); the tuned value (2.41×10⁻¹² s⁻¹) is 3.0× the measured 0.8×10⁻¹² s⁻¹, so the toy's absolute ionisation is not a physical claim. The skewer file also carries the generating code's own τ (exact Voigt) for the reference view.

Convention
the mapping conventions of Real space → velocity space map, Peculiar-velocity sign convention; LOS along the box x-axis; peculiar velocities computed from the displacement field (never from fake_spectra's get_velocity, Exporting skewers from fake_spectra 2.2.4 — a velocity-convention compatibility note)
Assumptions
  • Zel'dovich approximation; no hydrodynamics
  • no shocks
  • no pressure beyond a Gaussian filter
Valid for
teaching only
Simplifications
  • Rescaling τ to an observed mean flux is standard practice in simulation analysis (fake_spectra ships a mean-flux rescaler); here it is done through Γ_HI.

¶ Parcels are a teaching decomposition of a continuous sightline

The three parcels a, b, c summarise three n_HI peak regions of the real toy sightline (HI-weighted position, width, column, temperature, velocity and gradient). They are not discrete clouds; Beat 8 dissolves them back into cells. A parcel has a size along the beam, so the velocity spread across it widens its line too: for a Gaussian clump of width σ_x, b_size = √2·|aH + dv/dx|·σ_x adds in quadrature to the thermal b. Beat 6's parcel carries no internal gradient (dv/dx = 0 there), so its size term is the Hubble flow alone, b_size = √2·aH·σ_x; for the parcel it starts from, b_size = 23.8 km/s against a thermal 21.4 km/s, so the drawn line is 32.0 km/s wide (b) — Beat 6's figure names both parts, and "show the physics" prints each and the drawn line's own width.

¶ Ink is optical depth, and the ink rendering performs Beer–Lambert

"Ink" has one meaning throughout: a contribution to optical depth τ, laid in velocity space (Beats 6–13); neutral atoms are drawn as dark dots and motions as arrows, never called ink. The ribbon is rendered by compositing ink layers of opacity 1 − e^(−τᵢ) over a backlight C₀, which yields the transmitted fraction (C − C_ink)/(C₀ − C_ink) = Π e^(−τᵢ) = e^(−Στᵢ): the picture performs the rule it teaches (checked pixel by pixel, The drawing performs Beer–Lambert).

¶ The stretching ribbon and the written shadows (Beat 5 representation)

In Beat 5 the quasar's light is a ribbon carrying its own labels (the wavelength each part left with), laid against a ruler of wavelength measured where the light is now, starting at 0 Å, so the stretch by (1 + z_q)/(1 + z_here) is drawn exactly (anchored at zero, every interval scaled). Lyα of the gas being passed is a fixed mark at 1215.67 Å. The gas along the line of sight is a schematic continuous field, not a set of separate clouds: a seeded Gaussian random field in ln Δ (correlation length ~7 Mpc/h comoving, σ = 0.9; far coarser than real structure, chosen to be visible on a 4.5 Gpc/h path), quieter near the quasar, with three density peaks set exactly for the narration (the selected one, placed where the toy stretch's deepest absorption falls on the forest's own wavelength scale, so its shadow has the same wavelength in Beats 5, 11 and 12; and z = 2.90, 2.81). Every cell writes at its own Lyα with strength ∝ Δ² (photoionisation equilibrium, Photoionisation equilibrium and the neutral-amount control) × ((1+z)/4)^1.6, normalised so ⟨F⟩ = 0.74 over z = 2–3; the forest therefore thins toward low z. Density peaks (Δ > 2.2, with their surroundings Δ > 1.3) are the "structures" the narration names and the reader can select. What each cell writes is drawn ~60× wider than a real forest line (6 Å Doppler width when written, versus ~0.1 Å for b = 25 km/s); shadows combine by Beer–Lambert. The close-up of the mark is magnified ~20×. The surface spectrum is continuum-normalised; the quasar's Lyα emission (a schematic bump) is drawn only with "show the physics". The light packet's drawn wavelength is proportional to its true stretch. Path positions are comoving distances (Comoving distance along the light's path (Planck 2018)).

Convention
Cosmological redshift stretches every wavelength by the same factor, The forest is written along the way

6 · Inference: reading the forest backwards

Tracing a colour back to the gas, and why different gas can leave the same shadow — what breaks the tie, and where the inverse problem stays open.

¶ The "same shadow" configurations

A constructed degeneracy example, not a model of typical forest absorbers: (i) one unusually hot, idealised compact gas clump (T = 4.5×10⁴ K, Hubble width 2.23 km/s — about 7 kpc proper, far more compact than typical forest gas — N = 2.5×10¹⁴, at rest); (ii) two cold clouds (T = 10⁴ K, Hubble width 12.8 km/s each, 78 km/s apart in Hubble flow, 9.75×10¹³ each, approaching at ±24.9 km/s); (iii) one cold cloud stretched along the line (T = 10⁴ K, Hubble width 11.15 km/s, N = 2.5×10¹⁴, +6.2 km/s extra across 1σ) give Lyα lines indistinguishable at S/N = 20 per 2.5 km/s pixel with perfect resolution (Δχ² ≈ 2.8 and 0.9 over 121 pixels; 17 and 5.4 at S/N = 50, where the blend begins to show). (i) and (iii) are exactly degenerate in any H I line in the limit of a Gaussian velocity structure. These are two different kinds of degeneracy. The blend (ii) is measurement-limited: higher S/N, resolution or wavelength coverage can break it. Heat against smooth motion, (i) against (iii), is information-limited for hydrogen: every H I line depends only on the line-of-sight distribution of velocity and optical depth, in which thermal and smooth bulk broadening of one species are the same Gaussian, so another H I line gives no independent distinction — a line of a different mass does (What breaks the degeneracy). The blend hides because its two components overlap inside the saturated Lyα core, where the transmitted flux is near zero however the optical depth is split (Saturation and the curve of growth); Lyβ, with a smaller f λ, is not saturated there and separates it (What breaks the degeneracy). The toy's residual for (iii) (Δχ² ≈ 0.9 at S/N = 20) comes from hand-tuning, not physics.

Δχ2=∑k(Fk(n)−Fk(i))2/σF2\Delta\chi^2 = \sum_k \bigl(F^{(n)}_k - F^{(i)}_k\bigr)^2/\sigma_F^2Δχ2=k∑​(Fk(n)​−Fk(i)​)2/σF2​

Valid for

Simplifications

¶ What breaks the degeneracy

Thermal width scales as m^(−½) while bulk motion broadens all species alike, so a heavier ion's line in the same gas separates heat from motion (Si IV: m ≈ 28 m_H). Lyβ (f λ 6.24× smaller) saturates differently and exposes columns hidden in saturated Lyα.

b2=2kTm+bbulk2,(fλ)Lyβ(fλ)Lyα=0.079142×1025.7220.4164×1215.67=0.160b^2 = \frac{2kT}{m} + b^2_{\rm bulk},\qquad \frac{(f\lambda)_{\rm Ly\beta}}{(f\lambda)_{\rm Ly\alpha}} = \frac{0.079142\times1025.722}{0.4164\times1215.67} = 0.160b2=m2kT​+bbulk2​,(fλ)Lyα​(fλ)Lyβ​​=0.4164×1215.670.079142×1025.722​=0.160
Assumptions
  • the gas holds silicon in this ion — the tie-breaker applies only if it does
  • the metal line traces the same gas (single phase)
  • a common non-thermal (bulk) width shared by both species — an assumption that need not hold everywhere (Rauch et al. 1996), and a stronger one for H I with a metal ion than for two metal ions
  • illustrative metal column
Valid for
Illustrative. Si IV separates heat from motion only where silicon is present in the same gas. Lyβ helps only in some cases: in real spectra it lies inside the Lyα forest of lower-redshift gas, so blending and contamination must be modelled; its smaller f λ makes it useful mainly where Lyα saturates; and it needs wavelength coverage down to 1026 Å in the absorber's frame. Like every hydrogen line, Lyβ cannot separate heat from smooth motion (The "same shadow" configurations).
Simplifications
  • the Si IV column is chosen for visibility
  • Lyβ is drawn as a clean line, without the lower-redshift Lyα forest it lies in
Sources
  • Rauch et al. 1996 — §3, Eq. (1) (arXiv p. 5): b_i² = b_b² + 2kT/m_i — two ions of different mass (C IV and Si IV) separate temperature from bulk motion
  • NIST ASD (Kramida et al. 2024) — Si IV lines output 1390–1405 Å (ASD v5.12, accessed 2026-10-04): 3s–3p ²P°3/2 at 1393.76 Å (vacuum), f = 0.513
  • NIST isotopic compositions — Silicon entry: ²⁸Si 27.9769 u, 92.2 % of silicon
  • NIST ASD (Kramida et al. 2024) — H I lines output 1025–1026 Å (ASD v5.12, accessed 2026-10-03): 1s–3p 2P°3/2 and 2P°1/2, Ritz λ 1025.72182505 / 1025.72296565 Å, f 0.052761 / 0.026380 (sum 0.079142; f-weighted centre 1025.72221 Å)
  • Wiese & Fuhr 2009 — Table 6, entry No. 2 (1s–3p), p. 578: f = 0.079142
  • Griesmann & Kling 2000 — Table 1 'Resonance transitions' (arXiv p. 5): Si IV 3s ²S1/2 – 3p ²P3/2 at 1393.76018 Å (vacuum, laboratory Fourier-transform spectroscopy) (secondary)

Each check is an automated test in the source repository; its measured values are written by the test, never typed. ¶ Voigt function accuracy pass

The app's Voigt–Hjerting function H(a, x) is compared with SciPy's Faddeeva function (wofz) on a 42 × 321 grid covering a from 10⁻⁶ to 1 and x from 0 to 2×10⁴.

¶ Toy sightline: line kernels, neutral fraction, and the mean-flux calibration pass

On the toy sightline, the spectrum as drawn (Gaussian thermal kernels) is compared with the same sum using full Voigt kernels. The neutral fraction at mean density is computed from the measured ultraviolet background and checked to be about one in 10⁵. The mean transmitted flux is a calibration, not a test: the toy's ultraviolet background is tuned so that its mean flux matches the observed value, which is why the toy's ultraviolet is about three times the measured one.

¶ Same-shadow degeneracy pass

The Δχ² separating the three “same shadow” gas configurations is recomputed independently with exact Voigt profiles.

4/4 checks; Δχ²(S/N=20): ii 2.79, iii 0.87; max |ΔF| vs an independent calculation 3.6e-05

Criterion: browser and oracle Δχ² agree to 5 %

id VAL-DEG-001

Measured values: report (JSON)

¶ Redshift and frames pass

Comoving distance χ(z) and its inverse are compared with SciPy integration (Planck 2018 parameters); the frame conversions λ_obs = λ_rest(1 + z) and their reverses, the quasar frame, and the correspondence of log-wavelength and velocity are checked.

6/6 checks; χ(z) vs scipy max rel 8e-11; z(χ) inverse 2e-09; frame conversions exact to 1e-16; Lyα at z = 3 → 4862.68 Å

Criterion: χ rel < 1e-7; |Δz| < 1e-8; identities to 1e-14

id VAL-RED-001

Measured values: report (JSON)

¶ Toy spectrum against the code that generated it pass

The app's toy spectrum, as drawn, is compared with the exact-Voigt optical depth computed by the independent code that produced the toy data.

the app (Gaussian kernels, as drawn) vs the generating code's exact-Voigt τ: max |ΔF| 5.8e-04; the app with Voigt kernels 3.2e-05; ⟨F⟩ 0.6804 vs 0.6804

Criterion: as drawn max |ΔF| < 1e-3; Voigt kernels < 1e-4; ⟨F⟩ to 1e-3

id VAL-TOY-002

Measured values: report (JSON)

¶ Tracing a colour back to the gas pass

In “Who ate this colour?”, the per-cell contributions traced back from a colour are checked to sum to the spectrum's own optical depth at every pixel; the share the display leaves untraced is recorded.

Σ of traced contributions vs the spectrum's τ over 2048 pixels: max relative difference 5e-15; τ in cells under the 1% display cut (kept in the ledger's “rest”): median 3.2%, max 24.8% of a pixel's τ

Criterion: max relative |Σ τ_j − τ| < 1e-12 at every pixel; thresholds read from the beat manifest

id VAL-INV-001

Measured values: report (JSON)

¶ One parcel, four separate variables pass

In “Where does one parcel land?”, place, own motion, temperature and neutral amount are each changed alone across their ranges and checked to change only what they should — where the optical depth lands, how wide it is, or how deep — and the comparison the scene prints is checked against a fine-grid calculation. The width and peak it prints are checked to be those of the line it draws: heat alone and the parcel's size (the Hubble flow across it) add in quadrature.

91/91 checks over 18 one-variable changes (cells and τ, fine grid and the scene's grid): place and motion move the centre by aH·Δx and Δv (max error 4e-07 km/s) at fixed FWHM and area; temperature changes FWHM² by 4 ln2 Δ(b²) (max rel. error 1e-04) at fixed centre and area; amount scales τ exactly (max rel. 2e-15) at fixed centre and FWHM. The width the scene prints is the drawn line's: heat alone b = 21.4 km/s and the parcel's size 23.8 km/s add in quadrature to the drawn 32.0 km/s (max rel. error 2e-04; peak 3e-04). Flux is not linear (recorded): N_HI ×2 gives τ area ×2 but equivalent width ×1.19 (τ₀ = 4.4); T ×2 at fixed N_HI changes it ×1.13

Criterion: cells: only the intended property changes (relative 1e-12); τ on the fine grid: centre within 1e-3 km/s of aH·Δx or Δv, FWHM and area within 1e-3 (relative) when they should not change, FWHM² increment within 1e-2 of 4 ln2 Δ(b²), τ ratio = N ratio within 1e-9 where τ > 10⁻⁴ of its peak; the drawn line's b within 2e-3 of √(b_thermal² + b_size²) and its peak within 2e-3 of N σ_v/(√π b); the scene's printed comparison, width and peak correct to their printed precision

id VAL-ORTH-001

Measured values: report (JSON)

¶ The drawing performs Beer–Lambert pass

In “Light multiplies”, each pixel of the drawn light table is read back from the canvas: its transmitted fraction equals e^−τ at that colour, within 8-bit quantisation.

Beat 10 ribbon read back from the canvas: max |T − e^(−τ)| 2.1e-03 over 1000 columns (8-bit bound 2.1e-03); mean 9.0e-04

Criterion: max |T − e^(−τ)| ≤ the 8-bit quantisation bound 0.5/(light − ink)

id VAL-REND-001

Measured values: report (JSON)

¶ Closure against fake_spectra pass (declared domain)

The app's real-space method is compared with fake_spectra 2.2.4 on controlled skewers; differences are decomposed by source, and the domain in which the app's method applies is declared.

in domain (one velocity per sampling element, b ≥ 2Δu; 25 cases): max |ΔF| 4.9e-03, |Δ⟨F⟩| 2.9e-04, |ΔEW/EW| 2.8e-03, forest P1D 0.17 % (k ≤ 0.05 s/km), 0.32 % (k ≤ 0.1); C8b compared with the exact reference (fake_spectra's own quadrature error exceeds half the tolerance). Outside the domain, stated not tolerated (max |ΔF| per test case, by case name): several velocities inside one real-space sampling element (unresolved velocity structure; C10 is a deliberately exaggerated 1D shell-crossing stress test): C10s0 0.14, C10s1 0.059, C10s2 0.13, C10s3 0.2, C3c 0.089, C4c 0.021; lines narrower than two velocity pixels (b < 2Δu); fixable by oversampling the skewer: C6a 0.45, C6b 0.21, C6c 0.049, C6d 0.46. The app's code vs its independent Python port: 6e-15 in τ

Criterion: declared domain (one velocity per sampling element, b ≥ 2Δu): max |ΔF| ≤ 0.01, |Δ⟨F⟩| ≤ 1e-3, |ΔEW/EW| ≤ 1 %, P1D within 1 % (k ≤ 0.05 s/km) and 2 % (k ≤ 0.1); where fake_spectra's own error exceeds half the tolerance, compare with the exact reference; out-of-domain cases listed with measured values

id VAL-CLOSURE-FS

Measured values: science/validation/closure/metrics.json in the source repository
